events.text: The abbot sends you to face the wall in the Bodhidharma cave for a season. Just you, a wall, and your mind.

effects.log: A season of nothing. At the end, a little less of you, and a little more.
Four thousand and six. The abbot sighs and sends you back for another season.

events.text: The kitchen monk has been cooking tofu for fifty years. You have never seen him practise, but nobody ever steals from the kitchen.

effects.log: His knife work is a martial art. You learn more chopping cabbage than in the training hall.
You are on the floor before you see his hand move. He gives you the bun anyway.

events.text: A Shaolin rule: no meat. Your stomach has opinions about this.

effects.log: Your body grows lighter. Your qi grows cleaner.

choices.text: Sneak a chicken leg in the village

effects.log: Delicious. A senior monk smells it on you and says nothing, loudly.

events.text: Senior disciples whisper about the eighteen bronze men who guard the gate. You hear the clang of their training at night.

effects.log: One day you will walk through them. Today you do push-ups.

choices.text: Ask a bronze man about it

effects.log: He speaks for the first time in years: "Soon." You do not sleep.

events.text: A young novice has run away down the mountain, homesick. The abbot sends you to find him.

choices.text: Find him and walk him home

effects.log: You carry his bundle and listen to him cry. He comes back willingly.
You tell the abbot the truth. The abbot nods. "Some roads lead back later."

events.text: Taiji at dawn on the golden summit, a hundred disciples moving like one slow river.

effects.log: For an hour you are water.

choices.text: Watch the master at the front

effects.log: He moves so slowly that you finally see how fast he is.

events.text: The Wudang alchemists need a helper to watch a furnace for seven days without sleeping.

ok.log: Seven days, one pill, one very grateful alchemist.

fail.log: You doze on the fifth night. The pill is a small explosion.

effects.log: Alchemy smells too much of burnt hair anyway.

events.text: Two Wudang elders debate whether the sword should follow the mind or the mind the sword. They ask you.

effects.log: One elder smiles, the other frowns. You have made a friend and an examiner.
Both elders stare. Then both smile. You are sent to the library as a reward.

events.text: A master tells you to watch the cranes on the lake for a month and report what you learn.

effects.log: You report: they stand on one leg to rest the other. He laughs: "Good. Now your stance."
They fly. So, eventually, do you, off the dock.

events.text: Pilgrims crowd the Wudang steps to pray. The sect asks disciples to guide them.

effects.log: You carry three grandmothers up the steps on your back, one at a time.
Very profitable. The elders are unamused. (10 taels)

events.text: Mount Hua's new-year feast: plain rice, one chicken shared between forty disciples, and enormous pride.

choices.text: Give your share to the youngest

effects.log: The youngest cries. The whole table goes quiet. The elders remember.
The best chicken wing of your life.

events.text: The plum trees bloom on the peak. The sword master says the Plum Blossom Sword cannot be learned from a book, only from the trees.

effects.log: Twenty petals, twenty angles. Your sword blooms a little.
You cut no petals. You are told that is the point.

events.text: The cliff path of Mount Hua: planks bolted to a sheer cliff. Disciples run it at dawn.

ok.log: Fastest in your year. The seniors watch you with new eyes.

fail.log: You freeze halfway. A senior talks you across, not unkindly.

effects.log: Slow is safe. Safe is still here next year.

events.text: Namgung disciples visiting the mountain laugh at your patched robes.

ok.log: Patched robes, perfect swordwork. They stop laughing.

effects.log: 'Our robes are patched,' you say. 'Our swords are not.' Even they laugh at that.

events.text: Mount Hua dreams of its old glory. The sect leader asks every disciple for one idea to restore it.

effects.log: The sect's coffers grow. Pride grumbles. Rice improves.
'Then win it,' says the leader. No pressure.

events.text: On Emei's golden summit, the sea of clouds below turns gold at sunrise. The nuns call it the Buddha's light.

effects.log: Something in you goes very quiet.

choices.text: Help the old nun carry her stool

effects.log: She tells you about her youth as a bandit. You never look at her the same way.

events.text: Emei's monkeys steal a sutra from the temple. The abbess sends you after it.

ok.log: You retrieve it from the tallest tree. The monkeys shriek in respect.

fail.log: The monkeys win. The abbess sighs and writes a new copy.

effects.log: A fair trade. The sutra is only slightly chewed.

events.text: A merchant in the valley is known for cheating widows. Emei's rule: merciless to the wicked.

effects.log: He repays with interest, terrified.
The magistrate is his cousin. Slower justice, if any.

events.text: Emei needles: thrown at a paper target in the wind until every one hits the same point.

ok.log: Ten needles, one hole. The abbess nods.

fail.log: The wind wins. Your needles are all over the mountain.

effects.log: You watch the wind for an hour, then throw. Better.

events.text: A young man climbs Emei asking to join, not knowing the sect takes no men. The nuns laugh, then look at you.

choices.text: Show him the way down kindly

effects.log: He thanks you and joins another sect. He sends Emei a gift every year.

choices.text: Tell him Wudang's gate is open, and write him a letter for it

effects.log: You write the letter. The abbess reads it first and adds one line of her own. Years later a Wudang swordsman bows to you on the road, and you only just remember why.

events.text: Kunlun training: cross the snowfield without leaving footprints.

ok.log: Three steps with no trace. The masters exchange a look.

fail.log: A trail of deep footprints and one embarrassed disciple.

effects.log: You see where the weight goes: nowhere. You understand, almost.

events.text: The thin air of Kunlun makes newcomers dizzy. Veterans say it makes the qi purer.

effects.log: Your lungs grow. Your qi grows with them.
You faint twice and grow strong once.

events.text: Kunlun stands apart from the quarrels of the plains. Some nights, the loneliness of the mountain is very loud.

effects.log: The letters take months. The writing helps anyway.
He has been lonely for forty years and is very good at it. He teaches you.

events.text: A snow leopard has been taking the sect's goats.

ok.log: You drive it off without killing it. The goats are safe.

fail.log: It drives you off. The goats are unimpressed.

effects.log: Stone walls, high and cold. No more goats lost.

events.text: In the Beggars' Union, rank is shown by knots in the belt. You have one. The elders have nine.

effects.log: A year of carrying messages across the empire. The second knot is tied.
'Nothing,' says an elder with nine. 'And everything.' Beggars love riddles.

events.text: Every beggar in every city reports to the Union. Today you learn which sect is secretly broke.

effects.log: Information is worth more when it is held.
Silver now, trust lost later. (20 taels)

events.text: The Union runs a soup kitchen in winter. Every beggar serves, even the elders.

effects.log: Your arms ache from ladling. A thousand people eat.
The kitchen never goes cold.

events.text: The Green Bamboo Staff: the Union's secret art, taught only to a few. An elder is watching you.

choices.text: Practise with a bamboo pole every night

effects.log: Your pole technique becomes the talk of the Union.
The elder, oddly, approves more.

events.text: A Namgung family dinner: forty relatives, strict seating, and every conversation about swords.

effects.log: You impress two elders and offend one. Normal for a Namgung dinner.

choices.text: Talk to the quiet cousin at the end

effects.log: She is the best sword in the family and nobody knows. Now you do.

events.text: The Azure Sky Sword: its first form is taught to every Namgung child, its last only to the heir.

effects.log: The patriarch passes and stops to watch. That is praise.
'When you deserve it,' says the patriarch. So, never, perhaps.

events.text: A Namgung cousin challenges you to prove you deserve the family name.

ok.log: You win and are toasted at dinner.

fail.log: You lose. The cousin is gracious, which stings more.

choices.text: Decline: the family name is not a prize

effects.log: The patriarch overhears and smiles for the first time in a year.

events.text: Tang family dinner rule: never touch a dish before the cook tastes it. The cook is an aunt of the house.

effects.log: She tastes every dish. She has survived forty years of dinners.
Nothing happens. She looks at you with new respect and some worry.

events.text: Rain of Ten Thousand Needles: the Tang's most famous art. Today an uncle of the house throws a hundred at a board. They spell your name.

effects.log: He teaches you ten. You spell "Ta".
Your needles spell nothing. The board forgives you.

events.text: A Tang cousin wants to marry an outsider. The family elders are appalled.

effects.log: The elders are furious. The wedding happens anyway.
The cousin stops speaking to you.

events.text: Every Tang must learn antidotes by taking the poisons. Today: a mild one. They say.

ok.log: Fever, then strength. You understand the poison from inside.

fail.log: Mild, they said. You are sick for a week.

effects.log: You study it until you could brew the antidote in your sleep.

events.text: The Jegal family arranges stones in the courtyard every morning. Today they ask you to walk through without disturbing any.

ok.log: Not one stone moves. The elders nod to each other.

fail.log: Three stones move. The whole formation shifts. Oops.

effects.log: From above it is a map of the stars. You understand a little.

events.text: The Jegal elder plays Go against six students at once and wins every game while eating lunch.

effects.log: You lose in thirty moves. He compliments your fourteenth.
He eats without looking. He sees everything else.

events.text: Maps cover every wall in the Jegal library: battles centuries old, each annotated with what went wrong.

effects.log: You see the mistake on the third day. The elders were waiting for that.
A map of the courtyard. It is not a battle. The elders frame it anyway.

events.text: Breakfast in the Paeng house is louder than most battles.

effects.log: You win the argument about sabres. You are one of them now.
Nobody notices. You get the most food.

events.text: The Paeng sabre dance: a whole clan in the courtyard, sabres flashing, singing an old war song.

effects.log: You nearly lose an ear. Best morning of the year.
Your voice is terrible. Your spirit is Paeng.

events.text: The Paeng rule: never retreat before a friend is safe. A cousin is trapped by raiders on the northern road.

ok.log: You bring the cousin home over your saddle.

fail.log: You bring the cousin home, and a scar.

effects.log: An hour lost, forty Paeng gained. The raiders never had a chance.

events.text: The roof of White Crane Mountain leaks onto the master's bed again.

effects.log: The master sleeps dry. He pretends not to notice. He notices.
Smarter, if less heroic.

events.text: The old master shows you a tablet listing the sect's great masters. The last name is two hundred years old.

effects.log: He looks at you a long time. "Then do it."
A war, a betrayal, a fire. Twelve left. Then fewer.

events.text: The White Crane Sword: slow, patient, and devastating when it finally moves.

effects.log: A month of standing still. Then one perfect strike.
The master sighs. "You are a sparrow, not a crane."

events.text: The stronghold sends you to collect the monthly toll from a village that has no money this year.

effects.log: The chief is satisfied. The village is not.
The chief never knows.

events.text: The Black Wind decides everything by strength, including who gets the last bowl of stew.

ok.log: Stew is yours. So is respect.

fail.log: Stew is not yours. Bruises are.

effects.log: Everyone stares. Nobody says anything. The youngest never forgets.

events.text: The Seventy-Two Strongholds meet in the forest. Seventy-two chiefs, seventy-two grudges.

choices.text: Keep your mouth shut and learn

effects.log: You learn who hates whom. Valuable.

choices.text: Speak for peace between two strongholds

effects.log: Surprisingly, they listen.

events.text: The Greenwood has a code: never rob the poor, never harm the old. A new bandit broke it.

effects.log: The chief punishes him in front of everyone. The code holds.
He learns the code in a very memorable way.

events.text: The Water Gang taxes every boat on the river. A poor fisherman cannot pay.

effects.log: Your boss frowns. The fisherman leaves a fish on your boat every morning after.
Rules are rules. The fish is very good.

events.text: Water Gang training: swim across the river at night, against the current, in silence.

ok.log: Silent as a fish. The elders approve.

fail.log: You splash like a buffalo. The whole river hears.

effects.log: Clever. The elders laugh and make you swim twice.

events.text: Hushed Lantern trainees spend a month without speaking a word.

effects.log: You hear things you never noticed. Footsteps. Breathing. Lies.
Your trainer does not laugh. You start again.

events.text: Your first practice target is a straw man in a dark room. The room is full of bells.

ok.log: Not one bell. The trainer marks your name.

fail.log: Seventeen bells. Everyone in the building knows.

effects.log: 'Cheating,' says the trainer. 'Good.'

events.text: The poison garden of the valley: beautiful flowers, every one of them a death.

effects.log: You learn which to touch and which to fear.

choices.text: Ask which flower is the deadliest

effects.log: 'The one you ignore,' says the master.

events.text: A Tang family scout is caught at the valley edge. The elders want to make an example.

effects.log: 'The feud is old enough,' you say. The elders let him go, marked.
The example is made. The feud grows.

events.text: The Blood Cult holds a ritual at the new moon. Everyone must offer blood.

effects.log: The elders nod. You feel cold for a week.
The elders frown. Acceptable, barely.

events.text: A fellow disciple whispers that the Blood Ancestor is a lie. He looks very frightened.

effects.log: He trusts you. Dangerous, both ways.
He disappears. The elders praise your loyalty.

events.text: From the Cult's mountain, the Hundred Thousand Mountains roll away forever, blue on blue.

effects.log: The mountains do not care about Orthodox or Demonic. Neither, for an hour, do you.
Somewhere past the mountains is where you came from.

events.text: The Cult tests loyalty constantly. Today a stranger offers you gold to betray your hall.

effects.log: It was a test. You passed.
Also a test. Also passed, with a note on your cleverness.

events.text: Two halls of the Cult compete to deliver the most victories to the Heavenly Demon this year.

effects.log: Your hall wins. You are toasted with red wine.
Fewer enemies inside the Cult is worth more than a toast.
